data.findingId: 465bf2e:docs/runbooks/ci.md:59:Rollback misses the required status chec
data.title: Rollback misses the required status check on master
data.detail: The PM decided (card c-a5d4fd) to make ci a required check on master. Once set, disabling or deleting the workflow leaves every pull request waiting for a check that never comes, so GitHub blocks every merge, including the one that deletes the workflow. Fix: first rollback step removes ci from the required checks; correct the closing lines. PR #8 code review, finding 1.

data.findingId: 465bf2e:docs/runbooks/ci.md:46:The failing step is not the last one sho
data.title: The failing step is not the last one shown
data.detail: GitHub lists skipped steps and the Post Run and Complete job steps after the failure. Fix: say to find the step with the red X; later steps show as skipped. PR #8 code review, finding 2.

data.findingId: 465bf2e:docs/runbooks/ci.md:54:npm test builds the tools first, so buil
data.title: npm test builds the tools first, so build errors show in step 3
data.detail: scripts/run-tests.mjs line 32 builds the tools before tests, so an esbuild error fails npm test with no test name. Fix: add one sentence to the npm test bullet. PR #8 code review, finding 3.

data.findingId: 465bf2e:.github/workflows/ci.yml:11:No timeout-minutes on the ci job
data.title: No timeout-minutes on the ci job
data.detail: GitHub's default is 360 minutes. A hung test keeps ci pending for up to 6 hours and holds the sprint's merge chain. The first run took about 1 min 40 s. Fix: timeout-minutes: 15 on the job. PR #8 code review, finding 4.

data.findingId: 465bf2e:.github/workflows/ci.yml:15:Checkout leaves its token on disk
data.title: Checkout leaves its token on disk
data.detail: No step needs git credentials, so pull request code has no reason to see the token. Impact is small: the token can only read a public repository. Fix: persist-credentials: false on the checkout step. PR #8 code review, finding 5 (optional hardening).

data.findingId: f1222f2:docs/runbooks/ci.md:39:Runbook says tests never send notificati
data.title: Runbook says tests never send notifications; the requirement is never show
data.detail: DA-03.2 says running the tests never shows notifications to the PM. After da-t2 and da-t3 the notify suite sends to a stub notifier on purpose, so 'never send' becomes wrong. Fix: 'so tests never show a real notification.' PR #10 code review, L1. (L2, the feat(tests) commit type, has no file line; it is fixed by squash-merging with the PR title.)

data.findingId: f1222f2:docs/runbooks/ci.md:40:Runbook overstates TH-19: a suite with a
data.title: Runbook overstates TH-19: a suite with a fresh env does not get the switch
data.detail: 'so tests never send notifications' is stronger than TH-19's residual: a suite that builds a child's environment from scratch does not get the off switch. Fix: 'do not send real notifications. A suite that starts a child process must spread process.env into its env.' PR #10 security review, F3 (optional). Fixed together with code-review L1.

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:36:stubEnv accepts the real notifier path (
data.title: stubEnv accepts the real notifier path (TH-19)
data.detail: Security F1 and code review finding 3 (same defect). stubEnv checks only that the path is absolute, so stubEnv('/usr/bin/osascript') or stubEnv(notifierPath(process.env)) turns notifications on with platform darwin. A da-t4 to da-t9 test that does this shows a real banner on the PM's Mac or on the macos-latest CI runner, and the da-t4 rule ('dispatch only with notifierPath(stubEnv(...))') does not catch it. Fix: also throw unless the path is inside the suite's temporary folder (dirname(resolve(notifier)) === TMP), and add one throws line to the TH-19 test. STUB and <tmp>/missing still pass. Stricter than the TH-19 text; the architect would update threat-model.md:120-125 and design.md:408-411.

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:50:TH-19 test does not refuse a bare progra
data.title: TH-19 test does not refuse a bare program name (TH-3)
data.detail: Code review finding 2. The test refuses '' and 'relative/x' but not 'osascript', the one relative form that spawn looks up on PATH (TH-3). The code throws for it today; the test would not catch a later, weaker check. Fix: add throws(() => stubEnv('osascript'), /absolute path/).

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:44:The off-switch check does not stop the s
data.title: The off-switch check does not stop the suite (TH-19 residual)
data.detail: Security F3. DA-03.2 is an ordinary test; when it fails, runAll still runs every later test. From da-t4 on, a bundle run by hand or a runner change that drops the env would run later tests and CLI subprocesses with notifications on. Fix: before the temporary folder is made, exit 1 with a stderr line when process.env.PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFY !== 'off'; keep the named DA-03.2 test. The alternative is to keep it as the TH-19 residual already in threat-model.md:124-125.

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:45:DA-03.2 test cannot tell the runner's va
data.title: DA-03.2 test cannot tell the runner's value from the shell's
data.detail: Code review finding 1. The test reads process.env only. If the PM's shell exports PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFY=off and someone removes the env line in run-tests.mjs:58, a local npm test still passes. CI catches it because ci.yml does not set the variable. Matches the design's test seam; no change needed in this PR. Option: a devops task sets PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFY: on in the CI job so the test proves the runner overrides it.

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:39:A test can override the notifier after s
data.title: A test can override the notifier after spreading stubEnv (TH-19)
data.detail: Security F2. { ...stubEnv(STUB), PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFIER: '' } (or undefined, or a removed key) makes notifierPath fall back to /usr/bin/osascript with notifications on. An env built from nothing (for example { PATH }) loses the off switch. Fix: a review rule for da-t4 to da-t9, not code: every env in tests/notify.test.ts spreads process.env or stubEnv(...), nothing overrides PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFIER or PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIFY after stubEnv, and every stubEnv path is inside the temporary folder. Check: grep -nE 'PROJECT_COMPANION_NOTIF|env: *\{|stubEnv\(' tests/notify.test.ts.

data.findingId: 932c730:tests/notify.test.ts:28:The stub's hold loop has no upper limit
data.title: The stub's hold loop has no upper limit
data.detail: Security F4. If a later detached DA-02.3 test is interrupted (Ctrl-C) before clean-up, the detached stub keeps polling the hold file with sleep 0.05 until someone kills it. In this PR the only held run is bounded by the 5 s spawnSync timeout and the finally. Fix: bound the loop, for example i=0; while [ -e "$STUB_HOLD" ] && [ "$i" -lt 600 ]; do ...; i=$((i+1)); done.

data.reason: 3 of 10 sprint tasks merged before the sprint starts; no decision overdue
data.body:
Bottom line: Decision alerts are on track. 3 of the 10 tasks in sprint 2026-w42 are merged before the sprint starts on Monday, and the 4th (the notification record) is in review.

Done this week:
- CI now runs on every pull request: npm ci, typecheck, the tests and build:tools (PR 8).
- A test run can never show you a notification. The test runner sets the off switch (PR 10). The notify test suite uses only a stand-in notifier, and it stops at once if the off switch is missing (PR 11).
- The notification record is built: one git-ignored line for each notified decision, written so that no planted link can send it outside the project. It is in review as PR 12.
- devolps is at 0.3.12. You can now delegate one sprint's merges and questions with /devolps:delegate. You did this for sprint 2026-w42, until 16 October.

Next week:
- Finish sprint 2026-w42: the notifier, the off switch and macOS check, failure messages, the alert from gate request and card open, and the proofs that a broken notifier never changes a command (tasks da-t4 to da-t9).
- When the last task merges, prepare the release and ask you for the release gate.

Risks:
- A real notification on your Mac during development — unlikely, and serious if it happens (test text on your screen). The off switch, the suite's stop, and a review rule on every notify test guard it. Owner: EM, checked at each review.
- A tracker-log merge conflict after each squash merge — certain to come back, low impact. Under your delegation the EM merges with git merge -X theirs and checks that no log line is lost, and stops if the check fails. Owner: EM.
- Two track cards still show as open although you confirmed the tracks (known bug ee2e49d6) — certain, low impact. Planned for sprint 2026-w43. Owner: EM.

Decisions needed from you:
- Publish this update — type /devolps:publish-update <week>, or tell me what to change — by Monday 12 October.
- Confirm the Bugfix track for the 3 proposed bugs (15753492, ee2e49d6, d5ebde85) — options: Bugfix as proposed, or another track — recommendation: Bugfix — by the sprint 2026-w43 planning.

data.findingId: ffaa857:lib/project/notify-record.ts:65:No test makes the .gitignore write fail
data.title: No test makes the .gitignore write fail with an error other than EEXIST (TH-13)
data.detail: Code review. Two wrong versions pass every test: line 65 ignoring every .gitignore error and appending anyway (TH-13 says nothing is appended), or line 64 deleted so the reason names the folder, not <folder>/.gitignore (design 3.3 reason table). Fix: a test, skipped as root, that makes .project-notify/ a real folder with an empty record.jsonl, sets the folder to 0o500, expects RecordError 'EACCES <root>/.project-notify/.gitignore' and record.jsonl still empty, and restores 0o700 in a finally. Blocks the merge until fixed. Security note N4 is the same gap.

data.findingId: ffaa857:lib/project/notify-record.ts:68:Opening a FIFO at record.jsonl blocks fo
data.title: Opening a FIFO at record.jsonl blocks for ever (TH-8, D3)
data.detail: Security F1. openSync(record, O_WRONLY|...) waits for a reader if record.jsonl is a named pipe; try/catch cannot catch a wait. After da-t7 every gate request and card open would hang. Git cannot store a FIFO, so it needs a tar archive or a local process. Very low likelihood. EM decision (questions delegated): fix now, the safe option: add O_NONBLOCK (no reader gives ENXIO) and refuse a non-regular file after fstat. N1 (O_NOFOLLOW does not refuse a hard link) is recorded, not fixed: git cannot plant one.

data.findingId: ffaa857:lib/project/notify-record.ts:84:readRecord follows symlinks and has none
data.title: readRecord follows symlinks and has none of appendRecord's checks (TH-21, read side)
data.detail: Security F2. readFileSync follows a symlinked folder or record. Today only tests call readRecord. A later metric command could read a planted link (an outside JSONL file, a FIFO, a huge file). EM decision: no code change now; rule for any non-test caller: harden readRecord first (lstat the folder, O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, require isFile) and the architect adds a D3 read flow to the threat model.

data.findingId: ffaa857:lib/project/notify-record.ts:65:An existing .gitignore, folder mode or t
data.title: An existing .gitignore, folder mode or tracked record is trusted as is (TH-13 residual)
data.detail: Security F3. Any existing .gitignore counts (type and content unchecked); modes 0o700/0o600 hold only for entries this code creates; a record git already tracks is not ignored. In other projects without the root /.project-notify/ rule, a cloned repo could commit .project-notify/.gitignore as a symlink or empty file, and git add -A would then commit the record. Impact small: titles and commands are already in the committed event log (TH-6). Matches design step 2. Not fixed. Accepting it as a TH-13 residual is the PM's call (design level), recorded for the PM.

data.findingId: 2861b2d:lib/project/notify-record.ts:45:The suite does not prove O_NONBLOCK on i
data.title: The suite does not prove O_NONBLOCK on its own
data.detail: Backend-engineer hand-off, PR #12 rework. Removing only O_NONBLOCK from OPEN_FLAGS still passes 14/14: the FIFO test opens a reader first (so it can never hang) and therefore proves the isFile check, not the flag. A scratch probe in a child process shows the open then waits (killed after 5 s). EM decision (questions delegated): keep it; the flag is checked by reading. A child-process test with a kill timeout that expects ENXIO can come later if wanted.

data.findingId: 2861b2d:tests/notify.test.ts:132:A skipped test prints ok (root, or no mk
data.title: A skipped test prints ok (root, or no mkfifo)
data.detail: Backend-engineer hand-off. tests/harness.ts has no skip state, so the root-only TH-13 EACCES test and the mkfifo-only TH-8 test return early and print ok. On this Mac and the macos-latest CI runner they run (uid 501, /usr/bin/mkfifo present). EM decision: keep; a harness skip result is a separate change to tests/harness.ts, outside this task.

data.findingId: 25652b9:lib/project/notify.ts:55:dispatch accepts a program path that is
data.title: dispatch accepts a program path that is not absolute (TH-3)
data.detail: Security F1 and code review L1 (same defect). For a bare name, accessSync checks the current folder while spawn searches PATH, so the checked file and the program that runs can differ; under npx, node_modules/.bin comes first. The module header claims TH-3 for the whole module. EM decision (questions delegated): fix in this PR, the safe option: the first line of dispatch throws DispatchError('path', null) for a path that is not absolute; test with a name that is not on PATH (pc-no-such-notifier), recorded as the one exception to the stubEnv rule for dispatch calls.

data.findingId: 25652b9:tests/notify.test.ts:287:A STUB_OUT or STUB_HOLD already set in t
data.title: A STUB_OUT or STUB_HOLD already set in the shell leaks into the suite (TH-19 hygiene)
data.detail: Security F2. The last dispatch test starts the stub with the inherited environment and assumes STUB_OUT is not set. With STUB_OUT set in the developer's shell, the stub writes the hostile text (inert) into that outside folder; with STUB_HOLD naming an existing file, a detached sh polls for up to 600 rounds after the suite ends. EM decision: fix in this PR: stop the suite at the top when STUB_OUT or STUB_HOLD is set, next to the off-switch guard.

data.findingId: 25652b9:tests/notify.test.ts:285:No test here proves that dispatch never
data.title: No test here proves that dispatch never waits
data.detail: Code review L2. The stub inherits process.env (no STUB_OUT), so it exits at once; removing detached, stdio 'ignore' or unref fails neither dispatch test. The PR body claimed 'never waits'. EM decision: reword the PR body; the no-wait proof is DA-02.3 in da-t8 (6042a875). By reading, lines 63-69 match design 3.3 exactly.

data.findingId: eba7e4f:tests/notify.test.ts:364:The sent test cannot tell the stub from
data.title: The sent test cannot tell the stub from the real notifier (TH-19)
data.detail: Security F1. The witness is the outcome and the record line, so a later edit that makes notifyDecision dispatch notifierPath(process.env) or NOTIFIER would start /usr/bin/osascript with the display script (a real banner on the PM's Mac or the macos-latest runner) and the test would still pass. EM decision (questions delegated): fix in this PR: a second stub in TMP whose output path is written into its script (not read from the env); the sent test waits for that file with a guard timeout, so such a regression fails the test.

data.findingId: eba7e4f:tests/notify.test.ts:349:No test checks that off and unsupported
data.title: No test checks that off and unsupported win over a failed lookup
data.detail: Code review L1. Every DA-03.1/DA-03.3 call uses a decision that is in the cockpit; a change that moves the lookup-failed check above rows 1 and 2 passes all tests, and after da-t6 card open with the switch off and a failing lookup would print 'not sent'. EM decision: fix in this PR: an unknown id with off (and with off plus linux) expects 'off' and a line with null title and command; with only the platform set, expects 'unsupported'.

data.findingId: eba7e4f:lib/project/notify.ts:102:The 'not an absolute path' and 'did not
data.title: The 'not an absolute path' and 'did not start' reasons have no test
data.detail: Code review L2. da-t6's named tests cover access, spawn (NUL) and lookup (EISDIR) only. EM decision: add both tests in da-t6 (it owns the reasons and the 'not sent' line): pid via stubEnv(<TMP folder>) and an async test that waits one setImmediate; path via an exported failureReason(new DispatchError('path', null), 'pc-no-such-notifier').

data.findingId: eba7e4f:lib/project/notify.ts:11:Threat-model wording: TH-16 control and
data.title: Threat-model wording: TH-16 control and TH-5 residual (info)
data.detail: Security F2/F3 (info). notify.ts now imports readCockpit, which reaches appendEvent through its imports; the TH-16 control 'does not import appendEvent' is true but no longer a guarantee (the lookup path was read and writes nothing; DA-02.5 in da-t6 is the proof). controlsToSpaces replaces exactly the design range; U+2028/U+2029 and bidi characters pass (only the id and paths vary). For the architect and the PM: reword TH-16's control and add the TH-5 residual. Also design 3.3 'All of its work is inside one try/catch' no longer describes the two-catch layout. No code change.

data.findingId: a569a34:tests/notify.test.ts:454:The DA-02.5 fixture never reaches the ap
data.title: The DA-02.5 fixture never reaches the approved-gate lookup path (TH-16)
data.detail: Security F1. DA-02.5 is now the only real proof of TH-16 (notify.ts reaches appendEvent through readCockpit's imports), but its project has one requested gate with no artifacts and runs only 2 of the 5 failed causes, so withStaleness/hashArtifact never run. A later change that appends a gate.stale event from the lookup would pass. EM decision (questions delegated): fix in this PR: an approved design gate on docs/a.md, plus runs for a changed artifact (sent), the artifact replaced by a folder (failed, lookup) and a folder notifier (failed, no pid, wait one setImmediate); also check that .project bytes do not change.

data.findingId: a569a34:tests/notify.test.ts:465:DA-02.5 failure message does not show wh
data.title: DA-02.5 failure message does not show which event line changed
data.detail: Code review (optional). The length compare plus every(...) prints only 'an event line changed'. EM decision: fix with the F1 rework: eq(after, before, outcome), which prints both line lists.

data.findingId: a569a34:lib/project/notify.ts:147:Info: reasons keep U+2028, U+2029 and te
data.title: Info: reasons keep U+2028, U+2029 and text-direction controls; the stderr write is outside the try
data.detail: Security F2 and F3 (info). controlsToSpaces replaces exactly the design range (C0 and C1); a gate subject with U+2028 can reach 'not in the cockpit: <id>', but the CLI already prints that subject on stdout, so nothing new is disclosed. The new stderr write sits outside the try/catch, so 'never throws' relies on process.stderr.write not throwing synchronously (Node reports write errors as events; not checked here); the record-not-written write has the same pattern. No change; recorded for the PM.

data.findingId: 68fd4a3:tests/notify.test.ts:469:A failing DA-02.5 test prints the temp p
data.title: A failing DA-02.5 test prints the temp project's actor.identified line
data.detail: Backend-engineer hand-off, PR #16 rework. With eq(logLines(root), events, label), a failure prints every event line, including actor.identified (git email, name, host of the machine running the test). Only on failure; locally it is the developer's own terminal, in CI the runner's values in the job log. The committed .project-log already holds this kind of event. EM decision (questions delegated): keep it; a filter can be added if the PM wants CI logs to never show an identity.

data.findingId: 1a1e256:tests/notify.test.ts:538:cliTest clean-up miscounts stub runs whe
data.title: cliTest clean-up miscounts stub runs when the record cannot be written
data.detail: Code review M1. The finally counts started stubs from 'sent' record lines. With .project-notify as a regular file (DA-02.1 notes), readRecord throws ENOTDIR in the finally and replaces the test's result; with a symlinked record (TH-21 CLI test) the stub runs but no line is read, so its late .argv/.done reach STUB_OUT during the next CLI test (flaky DA-01.4/DA-01.5 or decide()). da-t8 must test exactly these cases. EM decision (questions delegated): fix in this PR: catch readRecord errors per project; a test that breaks the record waits for its own stub with calls(n).

data.findingId: 1a1e256:tests/notify.test.ts:631:CLI DA-02.5 check misses an event added
data.title: CLI DA-02.5 check misses an event added with notify on and off alike
data.detail: Code review L1. Comparing the on-log with the off-log cannot see an event appended at a call site in both. EM decision: fix in this PR: record the event count right after cliProject() and check it grew by exactly the decisions' own events.

data.findingId: 1a1e256:tests/notify.test.ts:647:DA-03.4 test does not check the README s
data.title: DA-03.4 test does not check the README section
data.detail: Code review L2. The test searches the whole README; a paragraph moved to another section would pass. EM decision: fix in this PR: the nearest '## ' heading above the paragraph must be '## Gates, sprints and the PM cockpit'.

data.findingId: 1a1e256:tests/notify.test.ts:537:cliTest finally does not remove STUB_HOL
data.title: cliTest finally does not remove STUB_HOLD
data.detail: Code review L3. If a da-t8 DA-02.3 test fails while the hold file exists, the clean-up waits 10 s and the held stub writes .done up to 30 s later, during later tests. EM decision: fix in this PR: rmSync(STUB_HOLD, { force: true }) first in the finally.

data.findingId: 1a1e256:tests/notify.test.ts:504:CLI tests rewrite the PM's global projec
data.title: CLI tests rewrite the PM's global project index (HOME)
data.detail: Security F1 and backend-engineer hand-off. The child inherits HOME, so each CLI run calls registerProject and rewrites ~/.claude/project-companion/index.json without a lock (about 40 runs here); temp paths stay after the folder is deleted, and a concurrent run can drop a real project. EM decision: fix in this PR for the notify suite: HOME set to a folder in TMP in cli(). The gate, cli and devolps-phase3 suites have the same issue and keep CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (security F6): proposed as a follow-up task for the PM.

data.findingId: 1a1e256:cli/index.ts:1460:card open now reaches the unbounded arti
data.title: card open now reaches the unbounded artifact lookup (SR-8); TH-7/TH-8 proofs wait for da-t8
data.detail: Security F3 and F4. Each card open now hashes every approved artifact (join(root, ref) accepts .., no size limit), so a merged log naming /dev/zero or a huge file hangs card open after it prints its id; the off switch does not avoid it (the lookup runs first). The threat model keeps TH-7/TH-8 open until DA-02.1 and DA-02.3 pass, which are da-t8. Code is correct by reading. For the PM at the merge gate: merge da-t8 right after this PR (as planned), and raise the SR-8 bug (d5ebde85) to the next slot.

data.findingId: 1a1e256:cli/index.ts:1243:Track-card banners can show an /devolps:
data.title: Track-card banners can show an /devolps:approve command with free agent text (TH-11)
data.detail: Security F5. A track card's command is /devolps:approve track <subject> <recommendation>; subject and --recommend are free text, and --recommend is not limited to full|quick|bugfix, so 'the body shows the kind' does not hold for track cards. The cockpit already shows this; the banner widens its reach (lock screen). For the PM: a follow-up task to refuse --recommend outside the three tracks, and correct TH-11 (architect).

data.findingId: f4b65b6:README.md:207:README paragraph overclaims and does not
data.title: README paragraph overclaims and does not say what a banner shows
data.detail: Security F2. 'never changes the command's exit code' is not true while SR-8 is open (a hung lookup can end in a timeout); 'writes one line' can be two (not sent, then record not written); and it does not say the banner and record.jsonl hold the decision's title and command, which matters for TH-6 (lock screen, screen sharing). EM decision (questions delegated): fix in this PR (rule 12): 'up to two lines', no 'never', and one sentence on what the banner and record contain, naming macOS 'Show previews'.

data.findingId: 0020f65:tests/notify.test.ts:505:cli() drops spawnSync's error, so DA-02.
data.title: cli() drops spawnSync's error, so DA-02.3 cannot see a 20 s ETIMEDOUT
data.detail: Code review finding 1 (security agrees). With dispatch changed from stdio 'ignore' to 'inherit', the CLI still exits 0 at once, but the held stub keeps the stdout pipe open, so spawnSync returns at its 20 s timeout with status 0 and error ETIMEDOUT; DA-02.3 checks only code and stderr and passes, while every caller that captures output waits for the notifier (TH-7). EM decision (questions delegated): fix in this PR: `if (run.error) throw run.error;` in cli(); it also protects the other CLI tests and da-t9.

data.findingId: 0020f65:tests/notify.test.ts:684:The results of await calls(1) are not as
data.title: The results of await calls(1) are not asserted
data.detail: Code review finding 2 (security agrees). A change that skips the notification when the record cannot be written would make each calls(1) return [] after ~10 s, and DA-02.1 and TH-21 would still pass. EM decision: fix in this PR: eq((await calls(1)).length, 1, 'stub calls') at each manual drain.

data.findingId: 0020f65:tests/notify.test.ts:738:TH-5 CLI setup does not check the exit c
data.title: TH-5 CLI setup does not check the exit codes of gate request and gate approve
data.detail: Code review finding 3. If gate approve starts to refuse --via prompt:test, the test fails later with a misleading message; the SR-8 bugfix must update this test. EM decision: fix in this PR: assert both setup exit codes are 0.

data.findingId: 0020f65:tests/notify.test.ts:759:Two comments are wrong (readRecord and '
data.title: Two comments are wrong (readRecord and 'the one field')
data.detail: Code review finding 4. A symlinked record does not stop readRecord: it follows the link and skips the non-JSON line; and line 667 says 'the one field' but names two. EM decision: fix the comments in this PR.

data.findingId: 0020f65:tests/notify.test.ts:698:DA-02.3 does not prove detached: true (T
data.title: DA-02.3 does not prove detached: true (TH-7)
data.detail: Security S1. Without detached, the suite stays green; if a caller kills or waits on the process group, osascript could be killed before the banner shows while the record says sent, or the command could be held. EM decision: fix in this PR: the stub also writes its process group id, and DA-02.3 checks it equals the stub's pid (a new group).

data.findingId: 0020f65:tests/notify.test.ts:719:The PWNED check in the CLI DA-02.4 test
data.title: The PWNED check in the CLI DA-02.4 test can never fail
data.detail: Security S2. The stub never runs its arguments, so the check proves nothing; the 'runs nothing' proof is the darwin osascript echo test (line ~281) plus the fixed NOTIFY_SCRIPT. EM decision: replace the check with a comment that names the real proof.

data.findingId: 0020f65:tests/notify.test.ts:670:DA-02.1 at the CLI does not cover the la
data.title: DA-02.1 at the CLI does not cover the late 'error' event (TH-8)
data.detail: Security S3. The one TH-8 cause outside the try/catch (a folder as the notifier: no pid, late error) is proven in process only. EM decision: fix in this PR: add a folder-notifier run to DA-02.1 (did not start <folder>, same output as off).

data.findingId: 0020f65:tests/notify.test.ts:505:Info: stubEnv accepts a symlink by name,
data.title: Info: stubEnv accepts a symlink by name, and the suite has no early stop if the notifier override breaks (TH-19)
data.detail: Security S4 and S5 (info). A later test could put a symlink to /usr/bin/osascript in TMP and pass it to cli(); and a regression in notifierPath would show a real banner at the first sent test and keep running. EM decision: fix both in this PR (cheap): stubEnv refuses a path whose lstat is a symbolic link; the suite stops at the top when notifierPath(stubEnv(STUB)) !== STUB. Security S6 (absolute 'touched' paths in run.progress events) is the existing bug 15753492.

data.findingId: 3ff92b0:tests/notify.test.ts:707:DA-04.1 checks 'at' only as an ISO strin
data.title: DA-04.1 checks 'at' only as an ISO string, not the time of the call
data.detail: Code review 1. A change that writes a fixed time (module load, or new Date(0)) still passes; DA-04.1 says 'the time'. EM decision (questions delegated): fix in this PR: take t0 = Date.now() before the run and check t0 <= Date.parse(at) <= Date.now().

data.findingId: 3ff92b0:tests/notify.test.ts:681:The mkdir-race comment cites the design
data.title: The mkdir-race comment cites the design for a decision the EM made
data.detail: Code review 2 and security I1. Design 3.3 step 1 only defines 'lstat again once' (design.md:321-322); the window it leaves unguarded is between step 1 and step 3 (design.md:333-334). Leaving the re-lstat branch untested was the EM's decision in da-t9 (rule 7: wrong source). EM decision: fix the comment (the PR body is already corrected). The re-lstat branch is the only folder-symlink check on that path; keeping it untested is surfaced to the PM to confirm.

data.findingId: 3ff92b0:tests/notify.test.ts:720:The line-break test counts lines but doe
data.title: The line-break test counts lines but does not check the title or the stub call (TH-15)
data.detail: Code review 3 and security L1. A lookup failure (title null, outcome failed) or a change that cleans the line break still passes with one line; the calls(1) result is not checked. EM decision: fix in this PR: the record title equals 'Ship\nit?' and calls(1) returns one call.

data.findingId: 3ff92b0:tests/notify.test.ts:696:A local const cardId shadows the suite h
data.title: A local const cardId shadows the suite helper cardId
data.detail: Code review 4. A later edit inside the loop that calls cardId(out) gets a TypeError. EM decision: fix in this PR: use the helper (const id = cardId(card.out)).

data.title: Prepare release 0.3.0: launch checklist, version, release notes

data.reason: All 10 sprint tasks merged; release 0.3.0 waits for a track decision
data.body:
Bottom line: Decision alerts is built. All 10 tasks of sprint 2026-w42 (9 planned, plus the CI task) are merged, all 17 criteria are ticked, and banners now reach your Mac for each new gate request and question or track card. Release 0.3.0 waits for one decision from you.

Done this week:
- CI runs on every pull request (PR 8).
- Decision alerts, PRs 10 to 19: the off switch and a test suite that can never show you a banner; a git-ignored local record of each alert; text passed to the notifier only as arguments; the off switch and macOS-only check; failure messages that never echo decision text; the alert from gate request and card open; and the proofs that a broken or slow notifier never changes a command.
- Each pull request had a code review, a security review and QA. Every high or medium finding was fixed before you merged.
- devolps is at 0.3.12. You delegated sprint 2026-w42's merges and questions until 16 October.

Next week:
- Release 0.3.0: the launch checklist, the version number, the release notes and the changelog, then the release gate for you.
- Sprint 2026-w43 planning: the three proposed bugfixes and the follow-up tasks from the reviews.

Risks:
- The SR-8 slow artifact lookup is now reachable from card open: unlikely (it needs a merged log that names a huge file or a device), and serious if it happens (card open hangs after it prints its id). Bug d5ebde85 fixes it. Owner: EM, for the next sprint.
- devolps cannot merge under a delegation in this repository: unlikely to change by itself, low impact (you type /devolps:ship each time). Cause: no command marks a review finding resolved, and carried-forward branches bring in old findings. Owner: devolps maintainers.

Decisions needed from you:
- Release task 0da68d29 has no confirmed track, so its agents cannot start — options: /devolps:approve track 0da68d29 quick (may then need a short Quick spec), or tell me to place the release task under the decision-alerts epic (Full track, its gates already approved) — recommendation: place it under the epic — by Monday 12 October.
- Accept or reject the open security items before the release gate: TH-7/TH-8 as mitigated with SR-8 as residual; F3 (TH-13 residual); F5 (track-card text, TH-11); the untested mkdir-race recheck (TH-21); record readers split on newlines only (TH-15) — by the release gate.
- Confirm the three bug tracks (15753492, ee2e49d6, d5ebde85) and raise d5ebde85 to the first slot — by the sprint 2026-w43 planning.
- Publish this update: /devolps:publish-update 2026-w41 — by Monday 12 October.
